Saw u (the Thai two-string bass) is a Thai bowed chordophone, the lowest in range of the saw family, lower than the saw duang. Its soundbox is made of coconut shell with the opening covered in cowhide, the body is held vertically, and its two silk strings are played with a bow; the bow is placed between the strings and the player tilts it to sound one string at a time. Traditionally it is played sitting with the instrument on the lap, and it can play solo but mostly serves as the backbone of an ensemble; in Thailand it was once common in pi phat ensembles, and at the end of the nineteenth century it also joined the soft-mallet pi phat ensemble and was used in a particular form of theatre pi phat ensemble.
可靠證據顯示，泰式低音二弦琴的形制可能取自中國樂器，與兩弦樂器 hu hu 相似: The reliable evidence suggests that the form of the Thai two-string bass may have been taken from a Chinese instrument, similar to the two-string hu hu; it appears around 1782 in the Bangkok period, or possibly earlier, in the late Ayutthaya period of 1700 to 1767. It used to play in the pi phat ensemble with the other accompanying instruments, and at the end of the nineteenth century it joined the pi phat ensemble that uses soft-padded beaters, and the special pi phat ensemble of a particular theatre form. It resembles the Cambodian tro u, and in China it developed into the yehu.

椰胡音色深沉暗啞，帶有濃厚的東南亞異域風情。其音域位於弦樂器的低音區，音質溫潤而: The yehu has a deep, muted timbre with a strong South-East Asian exotic flavour. Its range lies in the bass of the strings, the tone warm and a little weathered, with a distinctive bleakness. Because the body uses a coconut shell as its resonator, the sound has a natural warmth, though it is not as clear and bright as a Western fiddle. Its resonance is more restrained, its volume relatively soft, its tone long-drawn and expressive. Beside the saw duang of the same family the yehu is lower; it resembles the Chinese hu hu but has more of a Thai national character. Its timbre sits between a voice and an instrument, able to express delicate emotional turns, and it is an indispensable bass foundation in Thai traditional music.

泰式低音二弦琴為弦鳴擦弦樂器，發聲部件包括音箱、弦與弓。來源載明音箱以椰子殼製成: The Thai two-string bass is a bowed chordophone whose sounding parts are the soundbox, the strings and the bow. The source states that the soundbox is made of coconut shell with the front of the opening covered in cowhide, that there are two silk strings, and that the bow hair is horsehair and must be rosined before playing. As for the materials of the neck, pegs, bridge and other parts, the source does not state them, so no guess is made.
泰式低音二弦琴通常出現在泰國皮帕特（pi phat）合奏中，與伴奏樂器一同演奏；: The Thai two-string bass usually appears in the Thai pi phat ensemble, playing with the accompanying instruments; after the end of the nineteenth century it also joined the pi-phat-mai nuam ensemble, which uses soft-padded beaters, and was used in the pi phat derk dam ban ensemble of a particular theatre form. Although it can play solo, it more often serves as the bass backbone of certain ensembles, suits slow to medium-paced melodies, and is less used for fast ones.
演奏時傳統上坐著，將琴置於膝上，琴身垂直。琴有兩條絲弦，弓毛置於兩弦之間，演奏者: Traditionally it is played sitting down, with the instrument on the lap and the body vertical. The instrument has two silk strings, the bow hair is placed between them, and the player tilts the bow to set each string sounding. The bow is usually of horsehair and must be rosined now and then to keep its grip. A beginner can first practise slow to medium-paced melodies, since the timbre suits such phrases; at the same time watch that the bridge at the bottom is very sensitive, and that its position shifting over time will change the sound. The instrument is fairly fragile, so avoid knocks and too much force.
